Old habits haunt Rangers in early McInnes tenure
description: Derek McInnes says Rangers were "guilty of beating ourselves" as he bemoaned the loss of cheap goals in the Europa League qualifying first-leg defeat to Jagiellonia Bialystok in Poland.
fullText:
Two games, no wins, and a whole lot of work yet to do - there has been no dream start for Derek McInnes in his dream job.

Rangers' 2-1 first-leg defeat in their Europa League third-round qualifier away to Jagiellonia Bialystok came hot on the heels of a meek draw at Dundee United in their Scottish Premiership curtain-raiser.

McInnes' appointment, many fans hoped, would be a fresh start for the club after a succession of managers who arrived with glowing reviews and bags of promise, before they all left under a cloud of criticism and disappointment.

Nine signings have arrived this summer, with more expected, but last year's ruinous form is casting a long shadow.

"We've seen a lot tonight of what I thought Rangers were last season," McInnes said after the defeat in Poland.

It's a damning indictment from someone who knows how high the standards should be at Ibrox.

Rangers' slackness punished in defeat by Jagiellonia

Rangers news, views and analysis

Neither Russell Martin nor Danny Rohl were able to restore past glories in their short stints in Govan while McInnes was taking Hearts to the verge of immortality.

Much of the condemnation surrounding the Ibrox club's failures last season came back to the same theme - they may be fluid and clinical going forward at times, but a soft underbelly put paid to hopes of success.

"I thought we gave up too many chances and gave teams too much encouragement," the 55-year-old added post match in Poland.

"We've got to be honest and say we are guilty of beating ourselves tonight. And that's no disrespect to our opponent because on transitions and counter-attack, it fuels them."

Rangers were flailing in the opening 45 minutes as Jagiellonia cut them open with ease, capitalising on numerous lapses in concentration.

Twelve minutes into the game, Thelo Aasgaard tried an audacious spin on the edge of the hosts' box, attempting to squeeze the ball through a small gap in the defence.

One minute later it was in the back of Rangers' net following an impressive counter.

"There's no bigger drain on confidence for any player, team, support than losing cheap goals," McInnes said.

"There were mistakes for the goals, and I understand that can happen, but we have got to be far more stingy with our work, defend the goal with our lives, don't give our opponent opportunities.

"At no cost is that ball going in our box, at no cost are they going to get a chance, and we've got to have a bit more of that approach to our work."

The central defensive partnership of Dujon Sterling and Emmanuel Fernandez looked particularly shaky.

"If you spoke to McInnes right now without a microphone in front of him, and you asked him, 'Do you trust Fernandez?', there's no way he says yes, no way," former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday said on BBC Sportsound.

"But he doesn't have an option at this moment in time to play someone else.

"I'm being very critical here, but I think Fernandez has every attribute to be a top, top central defender, yet it looks as if he hasn't had the education growing up of the basics of being a central defender."

Cammy Devlin, Findlay Curtis and Nicolas Raskin were introduced in a triple half-time change and they all played their part in a much better second-half showing from McInnes' side.

Curtis was the standout. The 20-year-old was a revelation on loan at Kilmarnock in the second half of last season, earning a call-up to Scotland's World Cup squad.

For a Rangers side crying out for attacking guile and inventiveness on the flanks, Curtis being limited to just eight minutes in their Premiership opener against United was surprising.

His 45 minutes in Poland - where he struck the post late on and flashed an effort just wide - surely will lead to greater involvement in a team short of attacking impetus right now.

"The second-half performance was better, in an attacking sense. Findlay Curtis had a large part to play in that," former Rangers striker Steven Thompson said on BBC Sportsound.

"He didn't have that first thought of, when he received the ball, laying it back or looking for a sitting midfielder.

"He wants to go and take people on. It's brilliant to see that, because there's not enough of that in this Rangers side. He put in a number of good deliveries.

"His performance was one of the major positives from the evening."

Halliday was similarly impressed, saying: "Curtis had a fearless nature to try to make a positive impact.

"Not everything came off, but when he gets the ball, he drives at players, he plays one-two, he's running off the ball and having efforts at goal.

"That alone sparked Rangers into that 5% or 10% more on the ball."

title: Brook's time will come as Test captain - McCullum
description: England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum backs Harry Brook as a future captain but says Joe Root will do an "amazing job" in his second stint.
fullText:
England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum says that Harry Brook's "time will come" as Test captain.

Brook, 27, is England's white-ball leader and was Test vice-captain but was overlooked after Ben Stokes' shock retirement as batter Joe Root was reappointed, having previously led England in 64 Tests between 2017 and 2022.

McCullum, who was sacked in July after a run of bad results and off-field incidents, backed Root's captaincy while Brook prepares the white-ball side for the 50-over World Cup next year.

"Everyone knows the affection that I have for Harry," McCullum told Sky Sports during London Spirit vs MI London at The Hundred.

"He's a wonderful player and he's doing a fine job as white-ball leader. I think his time will come in the Test job.

"I'm looking forward to working with him and hopefully growing and developing him into the leader that he can become.

"At some stage in the future, he will have a very important role in that capacity. But for now, Joe will do an amazing job."

Brook recently led England to a 2-1 one-day international series win over India, and has been in good form in The Hundred, striking a 15-ball fifty for Sunrisers Leeds earlier this week.

England's first Test against Pakistan starts on 19 August which will be Root's first back in charge, before Brook and McCullum will oversee three T20s and three ODIs against Sri Lanka in September.

Earlier today, England's squad for the first Test was announced with Ollie Pope and Dan Lawrence recalled to the side.

Drinking culture embedded in cricket - Stokes

Root in 'very different place' over Test captaincy

McCullum also gave his support for close friend Stephen Fleming, who has replaced him as Test coach.

Fleming, 53, will not be in charge for the Pakistan series as Marcus Trescothick will step in, meaning his first assignment will be the tour of South Africa in December.

"I had a great time in my four years but now it's going in a different direction, I think Flem will be excellent," McCullum said.

"He's a little bit like me, but better – that's how I would sum him up. He'll do a great job, and the ECB have done incredibly well to get someone like him to commit to English cricket for the period that he has. It's an outstanding achievement."

Fleming inherits a Test side that has recently struggled after a breath-taking start to the McCullum and Stokes era.

McCullum won 10 out of 12 Tests in his first year in charge but since then, England have lost 18 and won 17 of 37.

The duo will have to negotiate an increasingly busy cricketing schedule, and manage the priorities of players who play all three formats, which includes Brook.

"We talk pretty much every day, we're close mates," McCullum said of Fleming.

"We've done a lot together and he's one of those guys who I trust completely. We both just want what's best for English cricket.

"We want to set this up so that English cricket can be successful across all three formats of the game.

"That is going to take some give and take at times, we both understand that, but we will work very closely together and give everyone the best opportunity to get the success that we all want to see."

title: Trafford joins Leeds from Man City in potential £45m deal
description: Leeds United sign Manchester City and England goalkeeper James Trafford in a deal worth up to £45m.
fullText:
Leeds United have signed Manchester City goalkeeper James Trafford in a deal worth up to £45m.

The England international has left Etihad Stadium just a year after returning from Burnley in a £27m move last summer.

Trafford, who was part of England's World Cup squad this summer but did not feature, made 17 appearances for City last season - four in the Premier League - but played a big part in their Carabao Cup and FA Cup triumphs.

The 23-year-old's move to West Yorkshire comes after the arrival of Champions League-winning goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, in September, ended Trafford's hopes of establishing himself as Manchester City's first-choice goalkeeper.

The move represents a new record fee for a British goalkeeper, surpassing the previous benchmark of £30m which Everton paid Sunderland for Jordan Pickford in 2017.

It also makes him one of the most expensive goalkeepers in history, with only Kepa Arrizabalaga (£68m) and Alisson (£62m) commanding higher fees.

Could Leeds move help Trafford challenge for England keeper spot?

Pre-season with Farke reminds me of Klopp - Wilson

Barcelona? Real Madrid? Man City's Rodri has a decision to make

More than £80m has now been spent on Trafford in initial transfer fees.

As part of the deal taking him to Leeds, BBC Sport understands City will retain a 20% sell-on clause and have matching rights - meaning if they match a future offer for Trafford they will get first refusal on him.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke appears willing to pay a premium despite Trafford's limited opportunities at Manchester City last season, after both Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier left Elland Road this summer.

Lucas Perri and Alex Cairns remain on the books, though Perri lost his place to Darlow in the second half of last season and did not feature in the Premier League after a 4-3 defeat by Newcastle on 7 January.

Leeds are investing in the potential of a young goalkeeper whose highlights have largely come in the Championship with Burnley, where he conceded just 16 goals in 45 appearances.

Trafford has only played 32 top-flight games, but former Clarets boss Scott Parker previously praised his turnaround at Turf Moor before moving to the Etihad.

Praised as "world class" by Parker, Trafford's 29 clean sheets and 84.47% save ratio were key to Burnley's promotion back to the Premier League in 2024-25.

Trafford began his career at City and had loan spells with Accrington Stanley and Bolton Wanderers before joining Burnley in 2023.

He made 73 appearances for the Clarets before City activated their buy-back option last summer.

description: Micky van de Ven is close to agreeing a new five-year contract with Tottenham Hotspur.
fullText:
Micky van de Ven is close to agreeing a new five-year deal with Tottenham Hotspur.

The Netherlands international defender joined from Wolfsburg in 2023 on a six-year agreement that runs until 2029.

BBC Sport understands Van de Ven was considering his future in north London before the appointment of Roberto de Zerbi in March.

The arrival of the Italian manager, who helped keep Spurs in the Premier League, has been crucial in the 25-year-old's decision to seek new terms.

Record Spurs spend shows new ambition - Van de Ven

"It's really good that you can see the club has made some changes," Van de Ven told BBC Sport in July.

"You can see the club has a new ambition. It's something that's really important for players who have been here for a long time.

"Last season was a stressful season, unacceptable from our side, so to leave all of that behind and go into the new season fresh means a lot."

Tottenham have finished 17th in the Premier League in back-to-back seasons and their battle to stay in the top flight ran to the final day of the 2025-2026 campaign.

After a turbulent nine months featuring three managers, Van de Ven said he is looking forward to a brighter future under De Zerbi.

"It's going to be different compared to the manager we had last season," Van de Ven said.

"It's also going to be more enjoyable for people to watch because we'll be playing offensive football.

"It is something we needed because everybody was a little bit down."

title: Spirit eliminated after defeat by MI London

fullText:

London Spirit 160-5 (100 balls): Pretorius 52 (28); Sowter 2-29

London Spirit became the first team to be eliminated from The Hundred after a four-wicket defeat by MI London in front of a record crowd at Lord's.

Chasing 161, MI London needed an unlikely 70 off 37 balls but Sam Curran's 33 and a quickfire 32 off 16 from Sikandar Raza put them within touching distance.

Zimbabwe all-rounder Raza was making his first appearance of the campaign having replaced Rashid Khan, and smacked four sixes before he fell with just six needed to win.

Curran, who started slowly with one off seven balls before accelerating, laid the platform alongside Nicholas Pooran, who made 39 before he was brilliantly run out by David Willey to give Spirit hope.

But Raza led the counter-attack before Tom Curran and Ollie Pope, the latter newly recalled to England's Test side, held their nerve to complete the chase with six balls to spare.

The crowd figure of 27,721 was an all-time record attendance for a group stage match of The Hundred.

They had been entertained earlier in the day by Spirit opener Lhuan-Dre Pretorius' 52 off just 28 balls before the 20-year-old was sensationally caught by Will Jacks' diving relay effort on the boundary.

Willey whacked 31 off 18 and James Coles, who was the most expensive player at the auction earlier this year, made an unbeaten 30 as they posted a competitive 160-5.

But a lack of consistency cost them again, with just one win from six matches so far in a season to forget for head coach Andy Flower. Meanwhile, MI London move up to second in the table to boost their knockout chances.

title: Uefa says boycott may still go ahead as FA withdraws Infantino support
description: Fifa's backing of president Gianni Infantino at a meeting on Wednesday "changes nothing", says European governing body Uefa.
fullText:
European teams could still boycott competitions including the World Cup as Uefa says Fifa's defence of its president Gianni Infantino "changes nothing".

The English FA has sent a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino in reaction to the plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

European governing body Uefa said in a statement its conditions had not been met, despite Infantino's plan being aborted.

"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and secondly," Uefa's statement said. "Assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met."

Uefa has already said it has lost confidence in Infantino, calling the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal a "shabby, back room, opaque deal".

Infantino sorry for errors but stays Fifa president

If Infantino goes, who might replace him as Fifa president?

Infantino had offered all associations $40m (£30m) if they backed a proposal for private investment in its tournaments, including the men's and women's World Cups, through the FFE subsidiary.

World governing body Fifa said during Wednesday's meeting "mistakes" regarding FFE were "acknowledged", saying it was "not the intention" for the Fifa Council and members association to "feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently".

Uefa's statement in response added: "Uefa made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's announcement that some people employed by the Fifa president (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

Fifa has been approached for comment.

Infantino arrived at Fifa's offices in Rabat, Morocco on Wednesday in now-familiar fashion, chauffeured to the building in a motorcade, sitting in the back of a Mercedes with blacked out windows.

Some questioned whether he would still be the Fifa president when he left.

Yet if anything, on the surface at least, Infantino appears emboldened.

This was not the 56-year-old being ordered to a hearing to explain his actions.

It was Infantino who summoned members of the Fifa management board to sit around the table with him, to talk through the events of the last week.

Secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, Infantino's right-hand man, had been critical in an internal memo to staff, calling the FFE proposals "a sad and reproachable series of events".

After the meeting finished it appeared to be water under the bridge, with Infantino and Grafstrom pictured sat next to each other and smiling at a Women's Africa Cup of Nations match between Malawi and Zambia.

If there were clear-the-air talks, they appear to have worked.

Other members of the Fifa management board to attend the meeting included finance chief Thomas Peyer, legal chief Emilio Garcia Silvero, chief of staff Daniel O'Toole, chief of member associations Elkhan Mammadov and media relations director Bryan Swanson.

BBC Sport has been told that Fifa's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, was not invited.

Lamour strongly criticised Infantino's FFE plan, saying it was "the project of one person", and "the time has now come for football's political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions".

He added: "I lose my job, then so be it. At least I'll sleep well tonight."

Lamour has declined to comment to the BBC. Fifa has been approached for comment.

What concerns Uefa is that this meeting was a gathering of employees who are themselves part of the regime.

It is unknown if Infantino was forced to answer difficult questions about his plan. Questions such as: who was involved? Whether there was a competitive tender process? And if he stood to benefit personally?

While Fifa said "mistakes made were acknowledged" and an "apology was made", there was no direct accountability for the controversy.

Uefa still wants answers to those key questions and will not be content until it gets them - or Infantino leaves.

Uefa is in something of a pickle as it tries to get rid of Infantino.

The easiest route to success was the slow turning of the vice throughout this week, hoping to exert enough pressure to force him to quit.

Yet the Swiss appears to have no intention of walking away.

European football looks like an outlier, struggling to gain enough support to topple him.

On Thursday, Lamin Kaba Bajo, the president of the Gambia Football Federation, praised Infantino's "courage" and for the U-turn, and said he was "willing to give him my support more than ever".

Only Jordan, one of the few countries which did not back Infantino before last week, has publicly stated it will not vote for his re-election in March.

Concacaf, which oversees football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, also issued a public statement after the proposal was aborted but, unlike Uefa, it did not go as far as to say it had lost confidence in the Fifa president.

Conmebol, the South American confederation, said on Thursday it would not support "any action or procedure that disregards" Fifa's mechanisms before the presidential election.

The Confederation of African Football (Caf) said its executive committee "unanimously reconfirmed" its support for Infantino and thanked him for his support for African football over the years.

Ideally, Uefa would force an emergency meeting of the Fifa Council, to provide what it would consider to be a true chance to hold Infantino to account.

But getting the necessary 19 of 36 confederation and football association heads to support it has proven to be exceptionally difficult.

Uefa has also kept on the table the option of a vote of no confidence, which it can trigger via an extraordinary congress any time it wishes.

However, it would need a majority of Fifa's 211 member associations - 106 votes - to pass the motion. It would be a de facto presidential election without a second candidate.

If Uefa does not think it can get to 106, which looks a stretch, then there is little point in triggering the vote.

The other option is to try to find a unity candidate to stand against Infantino in the election next March. The favourite would be Concacaf president Victor Montagliani.

Any option which takes time gives Infantino space to build bridges, and with Fifa due to announce new funding to member associations by the end of the year he could dangle another carrot for his re-election.

Unless Uefa sticks by the nuclear option - and goes through with its threat of a boycott.

This has issues, and it is not a lever you can pull very often, otherwise it gives the impression of riding roughshod over the rest of the world.

It is one thing to use it to jettison the FFE proposal, another entirely to effectively dethrone the president with it.

Uefa's stance will soon be tested, with the Fifa Women's U20s World Cup kicking off in Poland on 5 September. Six European countries are due to take part, including England.

Some at the European confederation claim Wednesday's statement shows exactly why the beleaguered president must step down.

The feeling within Uefa is that the statement was far from representative of the entire world governing body, and that there has been a lack of consultation with the council or membership.

There is also a view that Infantino is trying to swerve personal responsibility by sharing out the blame for the aborted proposals, and that he alone should have apologised - rather than issue his expression of regret alongside his deputy Grafstrom.

In stark contrast, within Fifa, the view from one Infantino loyalist is that the outcry, especially in Europe, is bordering on "hysteria", and fails to acknowledge the legitimacy he has globally.

title: Vinicius Jr and Real Madrid agree new six-year deal
description: Brazil winger Vinicius Jr will stay at Real Madrid after agreeing improved terms with the Spanish side despite interest from Arsenal.
fullText:
Brazil winger Vinicius Jr has agreed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid that will keep him at the Bernabeu until 2032.

The 26-year-old had entered the final 12 months of his contract and attracted interest from Arsenal in recent weeks.

However, Real Madrid announced on Thursday the two parties have agreed to extend his deal to 30 June 2032.

Vinicius posted on Instagram: "Eight years at the Bernabeu are too short... Six more years, and then forever."

"Vinicius Jr has become one of the most important players in one of the most successful periods in our history," said the club in a statement.

Real Madrid sign Diomande in deal worth up to £120m

Barcelona? Real Madrid? Man City's Rodri has a decision to make

Talks over a deal were at an impasse until Real made a new offer on Wednesday, with Vinicius understood to be appreciative of the fresh terms.

He joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and signed a contract extension three years ago.

Real and his representatives have been in talks over a fresh deal for the past 18 months but he has now extended his stay at what he has previously called the club of his "dreams".

He returned to the club on Monday for his first pre-season training session and medical assessment following his World Cup campaign with Brazil.

Vinicius has scored 128 goals in 375 appearances for Real across all competitions, while he has 13 goals in 54 caps for Brazil.

He has helped Real win two Champions League titles, three La Ligas and one Copa del Rey during his time at the club.

It is understood Arsenal would have accelerated their interest in the Brazilian if he had rejected Real's terms but the Premier League champions must now look elsewhere as they target a left-sided forward.

Vincius' contract extension comes on the same day Real announced the signing of Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig for a fee worth up to £120m (140m euros).

Diomande is Real's sixth summer signing under new head coach Jose Mourinho, joining Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konate, Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella and Carlos Espi.

Real are also targeting Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri but now face competition from bitter rivals Barcelona.

title: Doku's new deal, Gonzalez to stay - what's latest on Man City transfers?
description: Winger Jeremy Doku is the latest Manchester City player to commit his future to the club after signing a new contract until 2031.
fullText:
Winger Jeremy Doku is the latest Manchester City player to commit his future to the club after signing a new contract until 2031.

Belgium international Doku joined City from Rennes for £55.4m in 2023 and sources have told BBC Sport the 24-year-old will extend his stay at Etihad Stadium, with an official announcement expected next week.

Doku played 48 times for City last season, scoring eight goals, to help the side win both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup in Pep Guardiola's final season in charge.

He becomes the fourth City player to sign a contract extension this summer after midfielder Phil Foden and defenders Josko Gvardiol and Abdukodir Khusanov all agreed new terms.

Midfielder Nico Gonzalez joined City from Porto for £50m last January but has struggled to hold down a regular first-team place.

The 24-year-old played 41 times in all competitions last season and scored a stunning winner in the FA Cup semi-final victory over Southampton, but he was in and out of the team for much of the campaign.

So far this pre-season, Gonzalez has played in both friendly matches, against Inter Milan and the K-League XI.

There were suggestions City may look to let him leave after just 19 months at the club, but the player himself has dismissed such suggestions.

"I'm happy here," said Gonzalez when asked about his future. "I don't want to leave and I think the club wants me to stay. I haven't seen anything but I'm happy here.

"When I play I think I do a really good job. A good example was the semi-final of the FA Cup when I did a good match. Every chance I got, I tried my best.

"The final of the FA Cup I was out but we won so it was an amazing day for me. If we win, I'm happy. My dream is to win trophies.

"If I don't play any matches and we win the Champions League next year, I will be so happy."

Approaching the second week of August and City have only signed one player, Elliot Anderson, who is likely to be in the first XI this season.

The fee paid to Nottingham Forest for the England international is a club record £116m, with the 23-year-old seemingly a replacement for Bernardo Silva, who departed at the end of his contract and joined Real Madrid.

Teenage winger Jeremy Monga may be given playing time in the academy after joining from Leicester, while goalkeeper Pierce Charles and winger Mathys Detourbet both immediately went out on loan after joining.

New boss Enzo Maresca said on Tuesday that director of football Hugo Viana and chief executive Ferran Soriano had both travelled to South Korea, where the team are currently spending pre-season, and the Italian admitted "we need to something" in regards to transfers.

Though there is an acknowledgement that they have not been as active as they would have liked, senior City sources say they are "relaxed" about the situation and have full "trust" in their transfer strategy.

It has been pointed out that Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi were long-term targets and were signed in January, deals that were brought forward from this summer and both have made a positive impact.

The squad is seen to be "young" and "exciting", one which claimed both domestic cups last season, with 20-year-old Brazilian Vitor Reis returning after a season-long loan at Girona and expected to be past of the first-team.

In terms of outgoings, Rodri is yet to sign a new contract and is now attracting attention from both Real Madrid and Barcelona, while fellow midfielder Tijjani Reijnders is likely to leave and has interest from Nottingham Forest.

Meanwhile, BBC Sport said last month winger Savinho is open to leaving the club with Tottenham exploring a move, yet nothing has materialised.

If there are departures from the club, the idea - as it stands - is to bring in a replacement.

There is interest in Chelsea's Pedro Neto, while talks are ongoing for Lille's Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi and Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli.

Despite the lack of movement, there remains an air of calmness around the hierarchy at the Etihad.

Wigan thrash Saints in opening Super Four game
description: Wigan Warriors kick off the new Super Four format of the Women's Super League with a thumping 44-6 win at St Helens.
fullText:
Tries: Derbyshire 2, Hunter 2, Davies, M Jones, Wilton, Foubister, Coleman Goals: Rowe 4

Wigan Warriors maintained their 100% record in 2026 as they comfortably saw off rivals St Helens in the first match of the new Super Four format.

It was a fifth successive win for them over Saints in the past 12 months, including a 54-6 demolition in the Challenge Cup final at Wembley, as they underlined why they are the team to beat in the Women's Super League.

The defending champions scored nine tries with two apiece for Ellise Derbyshire and Eva Hunter with further scores from Anna Davies, Molly Jones, Remi Wilton, Jenna Foubister and Mary Coleman at the BrewDog Stadium.

St Helens were outclassed on home turf and had only a Luci McColm try on the stroke of half-time on a difficult evening.

Whatever the format, though, there is no doubt that Wigan are the standard-bearers for the rest to catch.

They scored from their first set as a high kick into the sun on the last tackle was spilled by young Saints full-back Liv Leach and bounced invitingly for Derbyshire to score.

That was soon backed up by a fabulous individual try from Woman of Steel Hunter as she received the ball inside her own half and showed an irresistible combination of power, pace and sidestepping to score.

To make matters worse for Saints, Leach had to be carried off the field and by the 15th minute the contest was nearly over as Davies went over in the corner after a gorgeous kick over the top from Izzy Rowe.

Derbyshire and Hunter crossed for their second tries and only a poor conversion rate from Rowe prevented Wigan from being out of sight.

With this, Saints finally gained some possession and repeat sets and McColm went over just before the interval.

However, hopes of any kind of comeback never materialised as Jones' try on her first appearance of the season after a knee injury got Wigan moving again.

And the champions simply were too hot to handle in the final quarter as Wilton, Foubister and Coleman went over as Denis Betts' side picked up from where they had left off in their last match nearly four weeks ago.

This was the opening match in the new Super Four format introduced for the 2026 season.

After seven rounds of games, with all sides playing each other once, the league has been split into a top four and a bottom four although all points have been carried forward.

There are now six rounds of games over the next six weekends with home-and-away fixtures against the other three teams in their section in an attempt to have the best teams playing each other more often to increase competition and intensity.

So Wigan play Saints, Leeds Rhinos and York Valkyrie twice, with the side who finishes top at the end of that securing a direct place into the Grand Final, second and third having a play-off to decide who else reaches that game and fourth missing out completely.

Meanwhile in the Shield, for the sides from fifth to eighth after seven matches, the side finishing bottom at the end of the season will play the winners of the National Championship for the final remaining Super League spot in 2027.

title: Le Court wins stage six of Tour after mechanical failure
description: Kimberley Le Court wins a sprint finish to seal victory in stage six of the Tour de France Femmes on Thursday, as Swiss rider Marlen Reusser holds on to the overall lead.
fullText:
Kimberley Le Court overcame a mechanical failure before winning a sprint finish to seal victory in stage six of the Tour de France Femmes on Thursday, as Swiss rider Marlen Reusser held on to the overall lead.

Le Court of AG Insurance-Soudal, who also crashed early on in the stage, was forced her to change bike just 15 km from the end.

The Mauritian fought her way back into contention shortly before the day's final climb, forming part of a small eight-rider breakaway group 10 km from the finish.

Le Court, 30, had just enough performance left to launch a sprint with 300m to go, holding off French rider Cedrine Kerbaol on the line to seal victory, with Puck Pieterse of the Netherlands taking third place.

Movistar's Reusser retains the yellow jersey after the 153.4km ride from Montbrison to Tournon-sur-Rhone, holding a 12-second lead over Dutch rider Demi Vollering.

Friday's stage seven - the queen stage - on the nine-stage event is 146.8km from La Voulte-sur-Rhone to the summit finish at the famous Mont Ventoux in the French Alps.

This was Le Court's second stage victory in the Tour de France Femmes following her win in stage five last year from Chasseneuil-du-Poitou to Gueret.

Le Court said her team was "amazing" during her bike change, adding: "They brought me back slowly but surely to the bunch, and I got back on top of the [second-to] last climb, which was a really big effort.

"Then I just tried to stay patient and recover from this big effort.

"I had to close the gap myself and I was really, really dead, I was on the limit. I can't believe I still had the legs to sprint."

fullText:
The Detroit Tigers' winning streak came to an end on Wednesday night with a 4-2 loss to the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park. The bullpen day effort started strong, but Brenan Hanifee surrendered three runs without recording an out and the offense was Woo'd by the home team's pitching, resulting in defeat.

Taking the mound in the series finale for the Motor City Kitties is left-hander Framber Valdez, who started the month off with a fine showing against the Athletics in Sacramento. The 32-year-old registered his 11th quality start of the season, allowing a pair of runs on nine hits and two walks while striking out six over seven innings, earning his sixth win with an 8-6 final score.

Valdez faced Seattle earlier this season on June 5 in Detroit, tossing five frames of one-run ball on five hits and two walks while striking out five, plus a hit-by-pitch for his third win of the 2026 campaign in a 7-3 final.

For the Mariners, right-hander Bryce Miller will climb the hill looking to turn the page on a subpar July. If you Porcello out his seven-shutout-inning effort to start July, the 27-year-old put up a 5.48 ERA and 6.28 FIP across four starts, allowing 25 hits (five home runs) and eight walks while striking out 12 and hitting a batter over that 21 1/3-inning span, earning three losses in the process.

Miller tossed a gem against the Tigers back on June 6, serving up six shutout innings on just one hit and two walks while striking out nine to earn his second win in a 4-0 finale.

title: Macclesfield FC director resigns following suspension
description: Local businessman Rob Smethhurst stepped in to buy the defunct club but was suspended in June after being arrested a month earlier.
fullText:
The director of Macclesfield FC has resigned two months after he was suspended following his arrest.

Local businessman Rob Smethhurst stepped in to buy the defunct Macclesfield Town in 2020, and oversaw the club's rise from the ninth tier of English football to the National League.

The journey reached its pinnacle when the Silkmen defeated FA Cup holders Crystal Palace in what was the greatest upset in the competition's history.

Smethhurst's departure comes after he was suspended after his arrest in May on suspicion of a coercive control offence. In a statement, Macclesfield FC said he had "other personal interests" away from the club but remained a shareholder. Smethurst declined to comment.

Smethurst has openly spoken of how founding the football club "saved his life" from addiction.

His role at the club was key to "rebuilding his life", as was his partnership with long-term friend Robbie Savage.

The club said: "With the consent of Robert Smethurst, Macclesfield FC can confirm that Rob has formally decided to resign as a director.

"We respect the fact that Rob has other personal interests away from the football club, and by accepting his resignation, he is able to spend more time pursuing these."

It added: "The club wishes to clarify that while Rob steps down from his day-to-day governance on the board of directors, he will remain a shareholder.

"In this capacity, we look forward to Rob's continued backing as we get ready for an exciting new season ahead."

In June, he was suspended following his arrest in Wilmslow, Cheshire, on 19 May on suspicion of a coercive control offence.

He was bailed pending further inquiries, Cheshire Constabulary said.

At the time, he dismissed the allegations against him as "an absolute load of rubbish".

The club said in June that it was "aware of reports circulating" and Smethurst had "temporarily been relieved of all duties associated with the club while legal guidance is sought".

title: Dortmund boss gives injury update on trio
description: With Borussia Dortmund's pre-season preparations underway, captain Emre Can and defender Nico Schlotterbeck remain sidelined with no clear return dates.Can has been out since March after suffering a t...
fullText:
With Borussia Dortmund's pre-season preparations underway, captain Emre Can and defender Nico Schlotterbeck remain sidelined with no clear return dates.

Can has been out since March after suffering a torn anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), while Schlotterbeck sustained a medial ligament injury in his ankle during the World Cup.

Speaking during a media session on Thursday, BVB sporting director Ole Book confirmed that there is currently no timetable for the returns of the two key defensive players.

"Even for very experienced doctors and our rehabilitation coaches, it's extremely difficult to predict the future. I see both of them every day working hard in rehab, fully motivated. They also continue to contribute a great deal as leaders within the squad," Book said.

"So nobody can say exactly how much longer it will take. And I'm certainly not the one who can."

As for Carney Chukwuemeka, who picked up a knock during Dortmund's 1-0 friendly win over FC Tokyo last week, Book provided more positive news.

"Carney landed on his knee some days ago. I'm not too worried that it's anything serious. At least it wasn't an issue beforehand," he said.

title: Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch says network won’t redo NFL deal until after 2029-30 opt-out
description: Fox Corporation CEO Lachlan Murdoch broke some major news during his company’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday morning. After about a year of speculation that the NFL and its incumbent broadcast partners would engage in talks to renegotiate media rights deals several years prior to the league’s opt-out options at the end of the decade,…
fullText:
Fox Corporation CEO Lachlan Murdoch broke some major news during his company's quarterly earnings call on Thursday morning.

After about a year of speculation that the NFL and its incumbent broadcast partners would engage in talks to renegotiate media rights deals several years prior to the league's opt-out options at the end of the decade, with the upshot being that the NFL would earn more money from its broadcast partners now and, in exchange, remove its opt-out clauses, guaranteeing its partners remain in business with the league well into the 2030s, Fox has decided it will instead roll the dice and reengage with the NFL following the 2029-30 season.

Murdoch told investors that Fox "will not be making any amendments" to its current NFL media rights deal until the league's opt-out option hits following 2029-30. The Fox CEO added that the decision was made as a result of talks with the NFL.

Fox CEO: Decision a result of talks with NFL

— Brian Steinberg (@bristei) August 6, 2026

"We don't see any changes to our contractual terms until the 2030 season," Murdoch told investors later in the call, offering little detail about why or how this decision was made. "Our relationship with the NFL is an incredibly positive one. We engage with them all the time," he continued, adding he sees "a clear path forward" following the league's opt-out.

Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch said on the company’s Q4 earnings call just now that it won’t look to open up its NFL deal until after the 2029-30 season.

“We don’t see any changes to our contractual terms until the 2030 season.”

— Josh Carpenter (@JoshACarpenter) August 6, 2026

Fox CEO: Will take up rights talks much closer to the end of the contract. 'Very pleased' with recent decision to strike deal for Mexican rights and sees 'a clear path forward' after 2029

— Brian Steinberg (@bristei) August 6, 2026

The comments come as a considerable development in the league's effort to negotiate new terms to its broadcast deals, which the NFL sees as significantly undervalued in the current market for media rights. Fox's decision comes just days after reports surfaced that talks between the NFL and CBS had stalled on account of Paramount's impending merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Prior to Murdoch's confirmation that Fox's decision was a result of talks it had with the NFL, CBS was the only network to have been confirmed in active discussions with the league over its media rights.

Fox's decision perhaps shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Once the NFL made clear its desires to renegotiate broadcast rights early, angling to increase its annual TV revenue by billions of dollars, Fox launched a covert political pressure campaign reaching the highest levels of federal government, including the president. As a result, numerous arms of the federal government began scrutinizing the NFL's media business. The Department of Justice launched an investigation into potential anticompetitive practices from the NFL. The chairman of the Federal Communications Commission regularly opined on whether the NFL was running afoul of its antitrust exemption, which allows the league to bundle and sell its media rights to broadcasters in packages on behalf of its 32 franchises. Congressional hearings were held on the move of live sports broadcasts from linear television to streaming. Legislation was announced addressing the fragmentation of live sports broadcasts.

Whether any of these efforts had real standing to change how the NFL conducts its media business is unclear. But the onslaught of political pressure, at the very least, created a roadblock for the league that forced its timeline for negotiations to shift back.

Now, the question falls to the NFL's other broadcast partners. CBS will presumably still need to come to new terms with the league prior to the 2029-30 opt-out because of the change-of-control provision triggered in its current contract following Skydance's purchase of Paramount last summer. The NFL, if it chooses, could exit its CBS deal early because of that clause, whereas it is locked in with every other partner through at least the end of the decade.

Fox's decision, however, might convince the NFL's other partners — NBC, ESPN, and Prime Video — to wait until the league's opt-out options hit before renegotiating. At the very least, it would ensure their media rights bills don't increase by potentially billions of dollars in the interim years.

If that is the case, the NFL's efforts to redo its deals early could reasonably be seen as a major failure of the league. However, it opens up a whole host of possibilities for how the league might choose to restructure its broadcast deals a few years from now, when it can break clean and divvy up inventory in whatever way it wants.

The post Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch says network won't redo NFL deal until after 2029-30 opt-out appeared first on Awful Announcing.

title: Baker Mayfield lands ahead of Jalen Hurts in The Athletic’s QB tiers
description: Baker Mayfield tied Sam Darnold at No. 14 and ranked ahead of Jalen Hurts as he enters a pivotal contract season with Tampa Bay
fullText:
Baker Mayfield's standing among NFL coaches and executives should provide additional support for his belief that he deserves another lucrative contract from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Mayfield tied Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold for No. 14 in The Athletic's 2026 NFL Quarterback Tiers. Mayfield remained in Tier 2 and landed ahead of Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence.

Mayfield also received one Tier 1 vote from the panel of 29 coaches and 21 executives. The 50 voters placed 35 veteran quarterbacks into five tiers based on their ability to carry an offense and perform in pure passing situations.

The ranking does not place Mayfield among the unquestioned elite, but it reflects the respect he has earned since arriving in Tampa Bay. Mayfield has rebuilt his career with the Buccaneers after being traded by Cleveland and spending brief periods with Carolina and the Los Angeles Rams. He led Tampa Bay to three consecutive NFC South championships from 2022 through 2024 and earned two Pro Bowl selections. His 2025 season was more uneven, as the Buccaneers missed the playoffs, but Mayfield still completed 65.4% of his passes for 3,693 yards, 26 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.

That résumé became the foundation for offseason contract negotiations between Mayfield and the Buccaneers. The sides did not reach an extension before his training-camp deadline, and Mayfield has put the discussions on hold to concentrate on the season.

Mayfield will play the final year of the three-year, $100 million contract he signed in 2024. He is scheduled to earn $40 million in 2026 and could become one of the most prominent unrestricted free agents available in March.

The Buccaneers must determine whether Mayfield's success represents the standard they can expect over another long-term agreement or whether his 2025 inconsistency warrants caution. Mayfield, meanwhile, has an entire season to strengthen his negotiating position.

Finishing ahead of Hurts and Lawrence is notable because both quarterbacks entered the league with significant investments from their franchises. Hurts has reached two Super Bowls and won one, while Lawrence was the No. 1 overall pick in 2021 and signed a five-year, $275 million extension with Jacksonville.

Mayfield's placement does not guarantee that Tampa Bay will meet his asking price, but it shows that NFL decision-makers generally view him as a legitimate upper-half starter. His Tier 2 status also suggests the Buccaneers would face considerable risk trying to replace him.

Mayfield wanted long-term security before training camp. He did not receive it, leaving the 2026 season as his opportunity to prove that No. 14 remains too low—and that Tampa Bay should pay him accordingly.

title: Government-run grocery stores face renewed scrutiny after Chicago's experiment fizzles
description: Chicago spent $13.5 million on government-run grocery stores now on the brink of collapse after Save A Lot terminated its Yellow Banana agreement.
fullText:
The idea of government-run grocery stores is facing renewed scrutiny as Chicago abandons plans for a municipal supermarket, raising questions about whether taxpayer-funded markets can survive.

"Chicago's city-run grocery stores are on the brink of collapse after a Save A Lot terminated its licensing agreement with stores operated by Yellow Banana," Bryce Hill, director of fiscal and economic analysis at Illinois Policy, told Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

"So the city spent $13.5 million on these stores, but now they're on the brink of closing. They were meant to address food security and availability in what the city deems food desks, but this outcome should really come as no surprise," Hill said.

Experts Scorch Mamdani's Grocery Plan As An 'Illusion' That Will Have Taxpayers Footing The Bill

Rob Karr, president and CEO of the Illinois Retail Merchants Association, told Fox News Digital Monday that the experiment is failing in multiple areas.

"So what we're seeing, particularly in New York and Seattle, are proposals to having the government actually artificially lowering prices by using their general revenue funds to make those groceries 'more affordable,' The state looked at that here in Illinois and dismissed it because it's inherently flawed," Karr said. "It has failed everywhere it has worked because it doesn't recognize the realities of the marketplace."

Chicago officials ultimately shifted away from opening a city-owned grocery store, opting instead to support privately operated neighborhood markets.

The Center Square reported Sunday that the closure of seven Save A Lot stores on Chicago's South and West sides has reignited questions about whether taxpayer-funded grocery initiatives can improve food access in low-income communities.

Snap Food Stamp Fraud Has Nefarious Terrorism Links, Top Agriculture Watchdog Warns Congress

In the article, Nicole Huyer, a free-market policy analyst, said the closures underscore the shortcomings of government-backed solutions.

The outlet also reported that the stores, managed by retail platform Yellow Banana, closed after Save A Lot terminated its operating agreement with the company, pointing to financial challenges that included a significant decrease in SNAP purchases.

The developer for the Whole Foods in Chicago's Englewood neighborhood, which closed in 2022, received a significant government subsidy, relying on an $11 million Tax Increment Financing (TIF) subsidy from the City of Chicago.

When it closed, local outlet WTTW reported that state Rep. Sonya Harper, D-Chicago, said in a statement that she was disappointed in the development, as the store had said it was not about making a profit but about ensuring access to healthy food.

"I was proud to work with Whole Foods to bring a new location to Englewood because they claimed their decision was not based on profitability, but rather a desire to help provide access to healthy groceries for residents," Harper said in the statement.

Steve Forbes: 4 Ways To Fix What's Wrong With New York City And Stop The Exodus

Hill told Fox News Digital that the areas where government grocery stores are failing tend to not be friendly to business.

"Illinois and Chicago specifically is one of the toughest places to do business. So, Illinois has the second-highest property taxes in the nation," Hill said. "They're even higher in Chicago. Commercial property here is taxed at 250% more than residential property, which makes it tougher for businesses to operate."

"So, property taxes are out of control, which affect business margins as well," Hill added. "But on top of that, for consumers and for businesses, Chicago's total sales tax, which also applies to groceries, was just at an increase on Aug. 1. So the total sales rate in the city is now 10.5%. It's the second highest of any city in the nation. If the city's serious about helping businesses and residents in need, it should start there rather than wasting millions of dollars on projects that we know are going to fail."

Karr told Fox News Digital that cities should look at practical ways to make it easier for grocery stores to operate.

Chicago Pol Says Walgreens Should Be Charged With 'First-degree Corporate Abandonment' Over Closure Over Theft

"Instead of trying to use gimmicks, look at the real reasons why grocery stores are having a hard time staying open," Karr said.

"And frankly, the same applies to pharmacies," he added. "Although it's a little different because there's also pharmacy reimbursement at stake there. But when you look at grocery stores, what are your permitting processes? What are your licensing processes? What are your labor mandates? What's going on in your property tax? When you look at the city of Chicago and Cook County, we have the classification system where commercial and industrial carry two-thirds of the burden. That's a problem. You can't continue to pile those on and expect something to change."

Fox News Digital reached out to Yellow Banana and Whole Foods for comment.

title: Nolan Wells report includes photos of friends’ boats: Report
description: The investigation into the death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells is ongoing.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — A report from the United Cajun Navy includes photos of the three boats Nolan Wells' friends took to the island, according to TMZ.

TMZ released the report, which comes as an investigation into the 18-year-old football player's death continues. Wells was last seen on July 4 after traveling to Mississippi's Horn Island with friends. His body was found two days after he was reported missing.

The boats in the photo include the Triton, which took on water before leaving. Wells' friend, Warren Hudson, says the group begged Wells to return with them, but he decided to stay behind. The report states the boat left at 4:31 p.m.

The photo was taken by Katelynn Brochard, the report states. According to the report, Brochard said Wells was nowhere in sight when her group left around 7:30 p.m.

Horn Island is only accessible by private boat and has no communications equipment, shelters or other facilities. Much of the investigation has centered around Wells' whereabouts on the island prior to his death, and why he did not leave with friends, something his family said was out of character.

The report has the last confirmed sighting of Wells between 3:23 p.m. and 4:27 p.m., with questions remaining about his activities during that time.

The report also includes information about an "almost fight" video taken around 5:00 p.m., noting that witness statements dispute the idea that a man in the video was Wells, suggesting that it should not be taken as a confirmed sighting.

The report has been sent to prosecutors, law enforcement and the Wells family, TMZ reported.

title: DSA-backed candidate topples millionaire Dem incumbent
description: DSA-backed Donavan McKinney unseated Rep. Shri Thanedar in Michigan's 13th district Democratic primary, extending a wave of socialist wins nationwide.
fullText:
Donavan McKinney, a congressional candidate backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) in Michigan's 13th Congressional District, won his Democratic primary on Wednesday morning, unseating incumbent Rep. Shri Thanedar, D-Mich.

From primary candidates in New York like socialist Darializa Avila Chevalier and her victory over incumbent Rep. title: New York gubernatorial candidate urges 9/11 attendees to turn away from Mamdani during ceremony
description: Bruce Blakeman says attendees should turn their backs on NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani at the 9/11 memorial over his refusal to condemn "globalize the intifada."
fullText:
Bruce Blakeman, the Republican candidate in New York's gubernatorial race, said Wednesday that attendees at this year's Sept. 11 memorial ceremony should turn their backs on New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani if he attends.

"I would equate this to a wake. You don't go to a wake if you're not welcome," Blakeman, whose nephew was killed in the South Tower on Sept. 11, 2001, and who currently serves as Nassau County executive, told reporters.

"I think it's completely appropriate if family members ask him not to come, but if he does come, I think there's a respectful and peaceful way to protest that, and I would suggest that people turn their back on the mayor," he said.

Firefighter Brother Of 9/11 Victim Incensed By 'Radical' Muslims Winning Key Dem Primaries

Blakeman argued Mamdani's refusal to condemn the phrase "globalize the intifada" should disqualify him from attending the ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks.

"He's not welcome there because he has yet to say anything in opposition to the global intifada. As a matter of fact, it seems like he supports that phrase, which is part of the reason why we had the tragedy we had on 9/11," Blakeman said.

Mamdani's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

The mayor has said he still plans to attend the ceremony.

9/11 Families Push To Ban Mamdani From 25Th Anniversary Remembrance Over 'Hostile' Record

"I will proudly honor the families, the survivors, the first responders forever impacted by that horrific terror attack by standing alongside them at this year's 9/11 commemoration — reaffirming that we will never forget the solemn day..." Mamdani said last week.

His comments came after relatives of Sept. 11 victims launched a petition urging the National September 11 Memorial & Museum to bar Mamdani from attending the ceremony in Lower Manhattan.

"Concerns have been raised about Mr. Mamdani's public positions, associations, and responses to rhetoric that many perceive as hostile to these shared values," the Change.org petition states.

"Given these concerns, we respectfully ask that the organizers carefully consider whether Mr. Mamdani's participation would align with the intention of the ceremony and the expectations of the families most directly affected by the tragedy."

Jewish Leaders Fault Mamdani Rhetoric As Upper West Side Stabbing, Hate Crime Probe Continues

A spokesperson for the 9/11 Memorial & Museum previously told Fox News Digital that the organization has "intentionally worked to keep the commemoration free of politics because remembering those we lost on 9/11 should never be a partisan issue."

"Government officials from across the political spectrum, including every sitting president, governor, and mayor since 9/11, have attended the ceremony simply to bear witness — they do not deliver remarks and are asked to remain in a designated area," the spokesperson added.

Former New York Gov. George Pataki was also asked Wednesday whether Mamdani should attend the ceremony.

"It's my nature to be inclusive, and that is my instinct, but Sept. 11 is different. So, I may have comments on that," Pataki said, according to the New York Post.

Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

title: Federal judge won't make disgraced clerk pay Alex Murdaugh's $600,000 in legal fees for 1st trial
description: A federal judge has thrown out a lawsuit by Alex Murdaugh seeking $600,000 in legal fees by the former court clerk whose misconduct led his murder convictions to be overturned on appeal.  Murdaugh sue...
fullText:
COLUMBIA, S.C (AP) — A federal judge has thrown out a lawsuit by Alex Murdaugh seeking $600,000 in legal fees by the former court clerk whose misconduct led his murder convictions to be overturned on appeal.

Murdaugh sued Becky Hill in May saying she violated his right to a fair trial in the deaths of his wife and son.

A jury found Murdaugh guilty, but the state Supreme Court overturned the convictions and life sentences earlier this year saying Hill's comments to jurors suggested the once-prominent lawyer was guilty and his testimony in his own defense couldn't be trusted.

The problem with Murdaugh's legal reasoning is he would have had to spend the money anyway because it wasn't Hill who investigated or pursued justice against him, Judge Richard Gergel wrote in his ruling Wednesday.

"Plaintiff's claim contains a fatal flaw — the lack of a causal connection between the funds he expended for his defense in the first trial and Defendant's misconduct. Defendant had no role in the initiation of criminal charges against Plaintiff," Gergel wrote.

Murdaugh's attorneys filed a notice to appeal about two hours later.

Murdaugh said in court papers he spent $600,000 from a retirement account to pay for his lawyers in his first trial and will need more money to pay them for his retrial next year in the case that has become a true crime sensation with a streaming miniseries, bestselling books and dozens of podcasts.

Even with his murder convictions overturned, Murdaugh remains in prison. He pleaded guilty to stealing around $12 million from his clients and is serving a 40-year federal sentence at the same time as a 27-year state sentence for his financial crimes.

His retrial on the murder charges has been scheduled for April.

Investigators said Murdaugh was addicted to opioids and his complex schemes to steal money from clients and his family's law firm were starting to unravel so he killed his wife and son to divert attention and buy time to find a way out of his problems.

title: No evidence? No problem. Trump pushes ahead on false claims that Reflecting Pool was vandalized
description: Jeanine Pirro this week found out there is a trade-off between loyalty to President Donald Trump and being loyal to reality.  The U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia — a fierce defender and dec...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Jeanine Pirro this week found out there is a trade-off between loyalty to President Donald Trump and being loyal to reality.

The U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia — a fierce defender and decades-long friend — openly refuted Trump's claims of vandalism regarding one of his treasured construction projects in the nation's capital, admitting in court filings that damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool was due to shoddy workmanship.

The moment comes as the Republican president is struggling to convince Americans that they should believe what he is telling them about the economy, his agenda and his war on Iran before pivotal midterm elections in the fall — and reveals the inherent challenges for his team in delivering hard truths he does not want to hear. Trump has historically engaged in exaggeration, but this was a moment in which he wanted a U.S. citizen, Olympic canoeist David Hearn, to be indicted, tried and possibly imprisoned for the act of touching a chunk of sealant in the already damaged pool.

The White House said that Trump was not aware ahead of time that Pirro's office would drop the charges.

Trump says he told Pirro he was "not happy" about her decision and that a video backed him up even though it is not clear from the footage shot at a distance that any property destruction occurred. "Well I just think she was totally wrong," Trump told reporters Tuesday night. "And everybody saw the vandalism."

"He just blows it up like a keg of dynamite — it's a form of intimidating employees to be in group-think," said Rice University professor Douglas Brinkley, a presidential historian. "'If you work for me, you triple down.' Never disagree with the boss, even in a small fractional way."

Trump has faced withering criticism for launching the war with Iran without fully laying out the rationale for the public or considering that country's ability to withstand intense bombing. Trump snubbed a housing bill to address the affordability problems that voters say are their biggest concern, letting it become law without his signature.

Some Republican lawmakers have suggested that Trump is being sheltered from facts or chalk up his choices to poor staff work. During Trump's second term, Republican senators including Ted Cruz of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina have said Trump was receiving "bad advice," a subtle critique of the president that shifts blame onto the aides who are supposed to be providing him with credible information.

The latest blow-up "reflects a president who is struggling to shape the narrative as his national approval ratings remain extremely low," said Julian Zelizer, a political history professor at Princeton University. "The more controversy that he faces — over Iran, the Epstein files, inflation and more — the less control he has and the stronger the chances that he will be forced to confront reality."

The president continues to dwell on the 2020 election that he falsely claims to have won. He likes to boast that America is booming with an unverifiable $19.2 trillion in investments from foreign countries, even as economic growth has been meager over the prior three months. He posted a Jesus-like picture of himself on social media and said after a backlash that he thought it depicted him as a medical doctor.

The White House did not respond to questions about how aides brief the president and whether officials feel comfortable providing information that could contradict his public statements.

Until now, Pirro, a former judge in Westchester County, New York, and TV show host, has largely been faithful to Trump's wishes. Her office sent a subpoena in January to the Federal Reserve regarding the congressional testimony by the central bank's then-chair, Jerome Powell, about a $2.5 billion renovation of its headquarters.

Pirro defended her decision to threaten Powell, who said the threat of a criminal indictment was really a pretext to pressure the Fed into slashing its benchmark interest rates in accordance with Trump's wishes.

"This office makes decisions based on the merits, nothing more and nothing less," Pirro posted on X. "We agree with the chairman of the Federal Reserve that no one is above the law, and that is why we expect his full cooperation."

Her actions temporarily slowed efforts in the Senate to confirm Kevin Warsh as the next Fed chair. The Department of Justice dropped the investigation in April, roughly a month after a federal prosecutor said in a closed-door court hearing that the government had not found any evidence of a crime.

On the reflecting pool, Pirro pursued the investigation despite what defense lawyers say was abundant evidence from the outset that the damage at the pool was the result of preexisting problems that had nothing to do with Hearn. A new court filing from Hearn's team disputes the department's contention that it only recently learned its case was flawed and urges a judge to not only dismiss it but to foreclose the possibility of ever resurrecting it.

"From day one, the case against Mr. Hearn was motivated by political considerations and devoid of adequate factual support," defense lawyers wrote. "Those political pressures have not dissipated in the mere four weeks since the government saw fit to obtain the indictment."

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche declined to discuss internal Justice Department conversations related to the case.

He deflected on the question of whether or not he supported the decision, acknowledging on one hand that Trump has "every right to be extraordinarily frustrated with damage done to our national monuments in this city and elsewhere" while simultaneously praising Pirro for what he asserted was "an unprecedented effort" to improve safety in the nation's capital.

"When you look at the D.C. U.S. Attorney's body of work over the past year and a half and where we are in this city compared to where we were, they are doing a phenomenal job," Blanche said. "Now does that mean that every case goes exactly the way that President Trump wants or I want or U.S. Attorney Pirro wants? Of course not, it doesn't."

What makes the reflecting pool incident different was that the administration contradicted claims of property damage made repeatedly by the president.

On Friday, the government moved to dismiss the criminal case and said any damage to the pool was caused by the bungled work of the contractor and "the rush to complete the project prior to events associated with the America 250 celebration in the weeks surrounding Independence Day 2026."

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum has supported Trump's claims that vandals damaged the pool. That suggests that the conflict around this issue could continue to simmer.

While Trump and many of his supporters are able to exist within their own information bubble, the administration had basically declared in court that the president was wrong. That was different from a judicial ruling or news report fact-checking him, said Kathleen Hall Jamieson, a professor of communication at the University of Pennsylvania.

"It's difficult to discredit that by saying these are anti-Trump forces," she said.

title: GOP infighting erupts as Thune warns of legislative ‘train wreck’
description: Internal squabbles erupted in the Senate Republican Conference on Wednesday as GOP senators battled each other and the White House over a variety of issues, prompting Senate Majority Leader John Thune...
fullText:
Internal squabbles erupted in the Senate Republican Conference on Wednesday as GOP senators battled each other and the White House over a variety of issues, prompting Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) to warn that his colleagues face a potential legislative "train wreck."

Senate Budget Committee Chair Ron Johnson (R-Wis.) clashed with Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine) over Johnson's relentless push for a vote on a budget resolution to begin moving a third reconciliation bill before the August recess, according to GOP sources familiar with the meeting.

Collins, who is perhaps the most vulnerable Senate Republican up for reelection this year, told colleagues that diving into a floor debate and vote-a-rama on amendments to a budget resolution would be politically unwise.

The budget reconciliation process would allow Republicans to circumvent a Democratic filibuster, but it would also give Democrats the chance to force votes on an unlimited number of potentially embarrassing amendments.

Johnson warned colleagues Wednesday that as many as 10 or 11 Senate committees could receive reconciliation instructions, which could make a wide array of amendments germane and viable for adoption at a simple-majority threshold, according to a senator who attended the meeting.

"If we vote yes on the motion to proceed" to the budget resolution and "we got on it, we'd have to do vote-a-rama, and that's what people are worried about," said a GOP senator, who requested anonymity to discuss pushback from Republican colleagues to trying to pass a budget resolution before the August recess.

The senator said Collins pointed out those potential pitfalls.

"Can you imagine how many amendments that would be?" the senator said, noting Republicans might have to vote on proposals to restrict Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) or to permanently ban the $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund to compensate MAGA allies prosecuted under former President Biden.

Several other GOP senators, in addition to Collins, pushed back hard against Johnson's proposal to initiate a messy budget reconciliation process before the August recess.

Collins has said for weeks that she would prefer to provide funding for the Pentagon and farmers who are struggling because of low commodity prices through the regular congressional appropriations process.

She declined to comment on the arguments she made to colleagues at Wednesday's conference meeting.

"I'm not going to discuss what happened at lunch," she told The Hill.

Johnson, however, said after the contentious lunch meeting that he's "still working" to advance the budget resolution before the Senate adjourns for the August recess.

Thune confirmed after the lunch meeting that attempting to move another budget resolution would drag "a bunch" of other committees into the process, which would open up the floor to votes on all sorts of controversial issues.

Asked if he would even have the votes to proceed to a budget resolution, Thune replied, "Probably hard to say."

Thune also must navigate internal Republican disagreements over a continuing resolution (CR) to fund the government until Dec. 11 and a bill championed by Senate Commerce Committee Chair Ted Cruz (R-Texas) to reform the rules for compensating college athletes.

"It's kind of a train wreck, isn't it?" Thune quipped to reporters as he arrived at the Capitol on Wednesday morning.

GOP senators battled with White House legislative staff at Wednesday's lunch meeting over language the White House added to the CR that would delay the implementation of a ban on hemp-derived THC products such as delta-8 until December.

Republicans in the meeting described the discussion as heated after the White House blindsided GOP lawmakers with the addition.

Some Republican senators want to delay the ban on hemp-derived THC products, such as Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.), who has argued that it unfairly targets Kentucky's hemp industry.

Paul on Wednesday accused Republican colleagues of exaggerating the potential harm of those popular products.

"These busybodies in there that want to ban everything are jumping up and down. It's like they watched 'Reefer Madness' in 1937 and they believe the whole world's going to be hooked on marijuana," Paul told reporters for The Associated Press and "PBS NewsHour" after the meeting.

But other GOP senators are adamant about stripping the White House-backed hemp language from the government funding bill.

Sen. Ted Budd (R-N.C.) is pressuring GOP leaders to allow a vote on an amendment to the stopgap measure to strip the provision.

"Let me be clear: I will not back down. I will not waver. I will not stop until this life-threatening hemp loophole is closed permanently. We must strip this amendment from the [continuing resolution] & regulate these harmful substances for what they are—not what the industry wants to call them," Budd posted on the social platform X.

Other Republicans say they don't want to have another fight over it right before Christmas.

Sens. Mike Rounds (R-S.D.), Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) and Bill Cassidy (R-La.) indicated they would support Budd's amendment.

"I'd rather have the fight now than during the holidays," Rounds said. "I can't see why we should include semisynthetic hemp as a part of hemp itself as something that moves forward in the future. Let's just call it what it is."

Rounds said he doesn't understand why the White House is trying to delay the ban on hemp-derived THC products.

"If I don't know and nobody's got a good reason for it, let's take it out of the bill and then let's get on with the CR," he added.

Thune also has to referee a Republican-versus-Republican fight over the Protect College Sports Act, a bipartisan bill drafted by Cruz and Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) to create new regulations for compensating college athletes for the use of their name, image and likeness.

Thune on Wednesday filed a cloture motion to advance the bill, but it faces an objection from Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.).

Hawley warns the legislation could overturn state-enacted bans on transgender athletes participating in women's sports.

"I'm concerned about that," Hawley said of Thune's effort to move forward on the college sports bill.

"I filed amendments to the bill. Listen, I'm against men in women's sports, and Missouri has a law that bans men in women's sports that applies to collegiate eligibility," he said.

"My concern is that this [bill] as it's currently drafted would overturn Missouri law. Twenty-seven states have similar bans. This is something that needs to be fixed," he added. "We cannot overturn 27 state laws that ban men in women's sports.

"That's just unthinkable," he declared. "Can you imagine a Republican Congress overturning Republican state laws that ban biological men in women's sports?"

Cruz, however, disputed the criticism that the bill would undermine state bans on transgender athletes in women's sports.

"That's simply inaccurate. The legislation explicitly has language, number one, that nothing in the bill alters Title IX in any way. And, number two, it explicitly says on eligibility that you can be blocked from eligibility for violating a state law," Cruz said. "That was written very deliberately to avoid disturbing the 27 states that have acted to protect women's sports."

Title IX is the civil rights law that prohibits sex-based discrimination in any education program.

Thune said he hopes the fight over the college sports reform bill won't stop it from passing before the August recess.

"I'm hoping it can be worked out. I know what it's about and I think … some of our members have pretty good answers to some of the questions he's raising," Thune said of Hawley's objection. "I'm hopeful that we'll have the bipartisan votes to get on the bill."

Thune also filed a cloture motion Wednesday to advance the House-passed ban on members of Congress trading stocks.

The legislation includes a provision that would require voters to show photo identification for federal elections.

Some GOP senators want to consider the House-approved stock-trading ban before the recess if they can't make progress on a budget resolution to pave the way for $10 billion in funding for states to tighten voting rules.

The Stop Insider Trading Act passed the House last month 232-198.

"It's a vote that a lot of members thought would be a good one to have. We're just teeing some things up," he said. "How it all unfolds is still a little bit up in the air."
